title: Finite-cover triple sites descend along affine inverse limits
statement:
Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category [def-weil-size-convention] and let $(X_i\to S_i\leftarrow Y_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes and arrows [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with affine transition morphisms in all three components. Let $X,S,Y$ be its componentwise limits. Write $\mathcal T_i$ and $\mathcal T$ for the finite-cover triple sites for the stage diagrams and the limit diagram in [lem-trf-qcqs-oriented-triple-presentation]: objects are triples of separated etale morphisms of finite presentation, and the finite pretopology is the closure under finite composition of the three generating covering types in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Scheme base change means [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then:

(1) The limit schemes and their two structural arrows are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Every finite diagram of triples and arrows in $\mathcal T$, with finitely many specified relations, descends up to isomorphism to some stage. Any equality between two arrows descended from one stage holds at some later stage if it holds in $\mathcal T$. A finite family that covers in this finite pretopology descends, after increasing its stage, as a finite covering family.

(2) There are equivalent small site models $\mathcal C_i$ of $\mathcal T_i$, continuous finite-limit- and cover-preserving functors $v_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ for $a:j\to i$, with $v_bv_a=v_{a\circ b}$ and $v_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, and continuous finite-limit-preserving $v_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$ with $v_jv_a=v_i$, where $\mathcal C$ is equivalent as a site to $\mathcal T$. Their object and arrow set cocones are filtered colimits, and the finite coverings of $\mathcal C$ are precisely the transported finite stage coverings. Thus this is a colimit site system of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites].

(3) Put $P_i=(X_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(S_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(Y_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$, using [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Under $P_i\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$ and $P\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, the geometric morphisms defined by $v_a$ and $v_i$ agree with the componentwise scheme-base-change geometric morphisms. These identifications respect the canonical identity and composition comparisons of inverse images and the adjunction units.
